paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God isn't impressed by what we SAY, He cares about what we DO. The chief priests and elders asked Jesus where His authority came from, but they had already dodged the answer in front of them. When Jesus asked about John's baptism, they said, "We do not know," and I think that was less about not knowing and more about not wanting to say (Matthew 21:25-27). Friend, you can't hear the truth when you're busy protecting yourself.

Then Jesus tells the story of two sons, and it turns the whole thing around. The first said no and went anyway. The second said "I will, sir," and never showed up (Matthew 21:29-30). I've been the first son plenty of times, groaning at the alarm and still making it to the ovens, and Jesus says that kind of person is the one who did the will of the father (Matthew 21:31).

So here's what it means for you, baker. It's never too late to change your mind and go, because Jesus says the tax collectors and prostitutes were entering the kingdom of God before the leaders, since they believed John (Matthew 21:31-32). But a polite yes with no follow-through leaves the work undone, and the leaders didn't repent even after they saw it happen (Matthew 21:32). Nobody is too far gone to turn around, and nobody is too religious to need to. And hang on to your apron, friend, because this story is not over.
